childNodes.textContent: Web MCP is a tool that lets AI agents control a real web browser on your computer. Think of it like giving your AI assistant the ability to open a browser, go to websites, click buttons, fill out forms, and read what is on the page.

It works with AI tools like OpenCode, Cursor, Claude Code, and many others. When you ask your AI to "go to google.com and search for something", Web MCP opens an actual Chromium browser window and does it right in front of you.
What you can do with it

attributes.aria-label: Permalink: What you can do with it

childNodes.textContent: Ask your AI to browse the web
— Your AI can navigate to any website, search for things, click on links, and scroll through pages. You can watch it happen in real time.
— Fill out forms, log in to websites, check dashboards, download reports. Your AI does the clicking and typing for you.
— Ask your AI to go through the checkout flow, check a specific page, or run through common user actions. Useful for quick testing without writing code.
— Your AI can visit a page, read the content, and summarize it for you. Great for research, price checking, or monitoring.
— Check your inbox, look at your analytics dashboard, review orders. The AI reads what is on the screen and tells you what you need to know.
— Chain together several browser actions. For example: go to a site, log in, navigate to a report page, download data, and save it. All from one command.
The install will automatically download a dedicated Chromium browser in the background. This takes about a minute.
and pick your AI tool from the list. This creates the configuration file your AI needs to talk to Web MCP.
Once setup is done, just ask your AI something like:
"Go to google.com and search for OpenCode"
Web MCP will launch the browser, do the task, and show you what is happening.
Everything stays on your machine. Web MCP runs entirely locally:
The browser opens on your computer, not on some remote server.
No screenshots, URLs, or browsing data are sent anywhere.
No analytics, no telemetry, no tracking.
Your actions and the AI's actions stay private to your session.
We designed it this way from the start. Your data is yours.
Web MCP works with these tools: OpenCode, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code (CLI), Windsurf, Zed Editor, Sourcegraph Cody, OpenAI Codex, ChatGPT Desktop, Cline, and Antigravity IDE.
The setup menu walks you through the configuration for each one.
For detailed guides, use cases, troubleshooting, and a complete list of available tools, check out the docs:
Built and maintained by Amit Narwal.

node.textContent: Web MCP is a tool that lets AI agents control a real web browser on your computer. Think of it like giving your AI assistant the ability to open a browser, go to websites, click buttons, fill out forms, and read what is on the page.

It works with AI tools like OpenCode, Cursor, Claude Code, and many others. When you ask your AI to "go to google.com and search for something", Web MCP opens an actual Chromium browser window and does it right in front of you.

attributes.aria-label: Permalink: What you can do with it

node.textContent: What you can do with it
— Your AI can navigate to any website, search for things, click on links, and scroll through pages. You can watch it happen in real time.
Ask your AI to browse the web
— Fill out forms, log in to websites, check dashboards, download reports. Your AI does the clicking and typing for you.
— Ask your AI to go through the checkout flow, check a specific page, or run through common user actions. Useful for quick testing without writing code.
— Your AI can visit a page, read the content, and summarize it for you. Great for research, price checking, or monitoring.
— Check your inbox, look at your analytics dashboard, review orders. The AI reads what is on the screen and tells you what you need to know.
— Chain together several browser actions. For example: go to a site, log in, navigate to a report page, download data, and save it. All from one command.

attributes.class: ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center

node.textContent: The install will automatically download a dedicated Chromium browser in the background. This takes about a minute.

attributes.class: ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center

node.textContent: and pick your AI tool from the list. This creates the configuration file your AI needs to talk to Web MCP.
Once setup is done, just ask your AI something like:
"Go to google.com and search for OpenCode"
Web MCP will launch the browser, do the task, and show you what is happening.
Everything stays on your machine. Web MCP runs entirely locally:
The browser opens on your computer, not on some remote server.
No screenshots, URLs, or browsing data are sent anywhere.
No analytics, no telemetry, no tracking.
Your actions and the AI's actions stay private to your session.
We designed it this way from the start. Your data is yours.
Web MCP works with these tools: OpenCode, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code (CLI), Windsurf, Zed Editor, Sourcegraph Cody, OpenAI Codex, ChatGPT Desktop, Cline, and Antigravity IDE.
The setup menu walks you through the configuration for each one.
For detailed guides, use cases, troubleshooting, and a complete list of available tools, check out the docs:
Built and maintained by Amit Narwal.
